description: Make `cam suggestions promote` variadic so shared-fix-site pen entries compose into one dedup-safe issue, and canonize the demand-driven pen-triage policy.

userStories.title: Variadic composite promote in one atomic on-main commit
userStories.description: As an orchestrator triaging the suggestion pen, I need `cam suggestions promote` to accept multiple fingerprints and file ONE composite issue carrying a dedup line for every promoted entry, so composing entries that share a fix site no longer regresses terminal-review dedup (the hand-composed promote-fp1+dismiss-fp2 path silently re-arms fp2).
acceptanceCriteria: `cam suggestions promote <fp1> [<fp2> ...]` accepts two or more fingerprints and files exactly ONE backlog issue whose description carries a `suggestion-fingerprint: <fp>` line for every promoted fingerprint. A new test named exactly 'promote composes multiple fingerprints into one issue' asserts both fingerprint lines exist in the single filed issue. [oracle: grep -q 'promote composes multiple fingerprints into one issue' test/commands/suggestions.test.ts]

All promoted pen lines are removed from scripts/cam/suggestions.jsonl in ONE atomic on-main commit (checkMainUpToDate guard + single commit-tree-to-main), while every non-promoted line is byte-preserved, and the composite issue description merges each promoted entry's derivedFrom/sourceIssue provenance, not only the first entry's. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Single-fingerprint `cam suggestions promote <fp>` stays byte-identical to today: one issue, one fingerprint line, exactly that one pen line removed, commit message shape `chore(cam): suggestions promote <fp> -> <id>` unchanged. The existing single-fp promote tests still pass. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

An unknown fingerprint anywhere in the argument list causes a non-zero exit and mutates NOTHING (no issue filed, pen file unchanged): all fingerprints are validated BEFORE any mutation (all-or-nothing). A new test named exactly 'promote with an unknown fingerprint mutates nothing' asserts it. [oracle: grep -q 'promote with an unknown fingerprint mutates nothing' test/commands/suggestions.test.ts]
The CLI arg-parse for the `promote` subcommand accepts a variadic fingerprint list and updated usage text. [oracle: grep -q 'promote <fingerprint>' index.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test test/commands/suggestions.test.ts]
userStories.notes: Core logic: `promoteSuggestionOnMain` (src/commands/suggestions.ts:533). Change the single `fingerprint: string` to a fingerprint list; validate EVERY fp exists via parseSuggestionsJsonl(readPenContentFromMain) BEFORE mutating (the current not-found guard at ~line 553 becomes a loop); `buildPromotedDescription` (~line 501) must emit one `suggestion-fingerprint:` line per entry and merge derivedFrom (resolveIssueId per entry's sourceIssue) and provenance lines for every entry; the `extraFiles` per-attempt callback must call `removeSuggestionLine` once per fingerprint against the fresh main content (keep the CAS-retry-safe recompute pattern, do not compute the rewrite once up front). Preserve `writeIssueFile` single-commit co-commit of issue JSON + pen rewrite. CLI wiring: `parseSuggestionsArgs` + `ParsedSuggestionsArgs` (index.ts:2115/2135) change `fingerprint: string` to a non-empty list and drop the `rest.length > 1` reject for promote (dismiss stays single-fp); `dispatchSuggestions` (index.ts:2231) forwards the list; update `SUGGESTIONS_USAGE`/help. Tests: test/commands/suggestions.test.ts (richer fake spawnFn at ~line 401 models commit-tree/hash-object). Gotcha (issue): dismiss removes a pen line WITHOUT filing, so hand-composing re-arms dedup; the composite path is the fix. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/index/regex access.

userStories.title: Canonize demand-driven + composition-by-fix-site triage policy
userStories.description: As the orchestrator consulting triage rules at pen-promotion time, I need the two-rule policy (demand-driven promotion + composition-by-fix-site) canonized in a memory/ decision file and its operative rule reflected in the orchestrator agent prompt, so the SHAPE of filed issues follows the operator's 2026-07-20 decision without re-deriving it each cycle.
acceptanceCriteria: The two-rule triage policy (demand-driven promotion + composition-by-fix-site) is canonized as memory/project_suggestion_triage.md per the knowledge-layer routing table in scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md (cross-cutting stakeholder policy -> memory/, NOT an ADR since it is cheaply reversible). [oracle: file-assert test -f memory/project_suggestion_triage.md]

The operative rule appears under the policy name 'composition-by-fix-site' in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md at the existing suggestion-triage section (~line 115) where the orchestrator consults it at triage time. [oracle: grep -q 'composition-by-fix-site' .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md]

The .claude/ and templates/ copies of subagent-orchestrator.md are diffed first and the edit is ADDITIVE to .claude/ only (they diverge by deliberate cam-cli specialization); no .claude/<->templates/ reconciliation is performed, and embed-vendor:check is run ONLY if templates/ was actually touched. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
memory/project_suggestion_triage.md contains no em-dash and no decorative emoji (persisted human-readable .md project rule). [oracle: ! grep -q '—' memory/project_suggestion_triage.md]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes: Files: create memory/ (does not exist yet) + memory/project_suggestion_triage.md; edit .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md ONLY (existing triage section ~line 115-120 documents promote/dismiss). Gotcha (patterns.md 'cam dual-copy is per-file' + 'Agent-prompt self-hosting pattern'): .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/ are NOT byte-identical and this issue explicitly says do NOT reconcile them; the edit is additive to .claude/ only, so templates/ is untouched and no re-embed/embed-vendor:check is required (diff confirmed: the two files already differ). Content: rule (1) demand-driven promotion (promote only when a cycle is about to touch the named surface; the pen is durable/committed so nothing is lost); rule (2) composition-by-fix-site (same file+rule+one coherent edit -> ONE composite issue; shared theme with independent fix sites stays separate; shared fate is the test, fix site the proxy). Persisted .md: no em-dash, no decorative emoji (project rule); agent .md may use em-dash but keep additive/consistent with surrounding prose.
